name: Gries am Brenner
kurzbeschreibung: Highest-lying municipality in the Wipptal, right at the Brennerpass, featuring the Brennersee ski area and the mountain hiker’s village of Steinacher.
beschreibung:
Overview

Gries am Brenner is situated at an elevation of 1,165 metres in the upper Wipptal along the Sill River in the Tyrolean district of Innsbruck-Land, serving as the southernmost municipality in the district directly before the 1,374-metre crest of the Brenner Pass. Covering an expansive territory of around 56 square kilometres, the community is home to roughly 1,350 residents dispersed across the main village of Gries and tranquil hamlets including Vinaders at the entrance to the Obernberg Valley, the sunny plateau of Nösslach, Lueg, and the Brennersee lake. Gries combines millennia of historic European transalpine transit with peaceful mountain seclusion in its side valleys. While highway and rail links traverse the valley floor, the surrounding mountain slopes around the Sattelberg and the Obernbergtal provide an unspoiled alpine sanctuary for hikers and ski tourers far from commercial resort crowds.

History

At 1,374 metres, the Brenner Pass is the lowest major crossing of the main Alpine chain, utilized since Bronze Age antiquity; around 200 AD, Roman Emperor Septimius Severus fortified the route as the military highway Via Raetia. During the Middle Ages, the road served as the Imperial Route (Via Imperii) for Holy Roman Kings journeying to Rome for coronation, as well as a vital merchant artery. The hamlet of Vinaders is historically older than the main village, first recorded in 1253 in records of the Bishopric of Brixen as an ancient pilgrim shelter. At the Lueg gorge, the Counts of Tyrol operated their most lucrative customs post from 1287 until its destruction in the Tyrolean uprising of 1809; the chapel of St. Christopher and Sigmund, founded in 1449 by Duke Sigmund the Rich, still stands beneath the viaduct. The parish church of St. Leonard in Vinaders, consecrated in 1490 and adorned around 1803 with frescoes by Josef Schmutzer, remains an architectural treasure. In 1867, the imperial Brenner Railway transformed travel, while today the monumental Brenner Base Tunnel project shapes the region.

Getting There

Gries am Brenner enjoys exceptional public rail connectivity: the ÖBB S-Bahn commuter line S3 operates hourly direct services from Innsbruck Central Station, reaching Gries station in just 35 to 40 minutes before continuing across the Italian border with connections to South Tyrol. By car, drivers use the Brenner Autobahn A13, taking either the Nösslach or Brennersee exit. Alternatively, the toll-free federal road B182 provides a picturesque route from Innsbruck through Schönberg, Matrei, and Steinach. Local bus route 4145 connects the station with the various municipal districts and runs deep into the Obernberg Valley.

Tips

A prime winter attraction is the 2,115-metre Sattelberg, one of North Tyrol's classic ski touring destinations, offering avalanche-safe forested slopes following the decommission of its old ski lifts. At 1,637 metres, the welcoming Sattelbergalm alpine hut serves traditional Tyrolean dumpling specialities year-round and features a prepared 4-kilometre natural toboggan run in winter. In summer, the mountain crest offers a historic ridge hike along ancient boundary stones marking the Austrian-Italian border. Outdoor lovers also stroll around the tranquil Lake Brennersee at 1,310 metres or venture into the neighbouring mountaineering village of Obernbergtal to marvel at the turquoise waters of Lake Obernberg beneath the Tribulaun peaks. The Bergeralm ski resort in nearby Steinach offers family-friendly downhill skiing and floodlit sledging.
metaDescription: Gries am Brenner in the Wipptal: Historic alpine pass village, Vinaders church, Sattelbergalm ski tours, Brennersee, and gateway to Obernbergtal.
